Description: Every microservice is registered once with its owner, environment, endpoint and version, and duplicate or malformed records are rejected (FR-002)
Architects map directed dependencies between services and explore an interactive topology graph for blast-radius analysis (FR-003, NFR-001)
Each service's OpenAPI specification is ingested, kept current and searchable in one place (FR-004)
Services are probed every 30 s at fleet scale, availability is computed, and downtime alerts are dispatched and audited (FR-001, FR-005, NFR-002)

As a DevOps engineer, I want to register a microservice with its name, owning team, environment, version, health-endpoint URL and repository URL, so that the catalog is the single source of truth for every service I run. (Requirement FR-002)

As a DevOps engineer, I want a submission whose name + environment already exists, or whose endpoint URL is invalid, rejected with a message that names the conflict, so that the catalog never holds ambiguous or broken entries. (Requirement FR-002)
As a system architect, I want to declare which services a service calls and which services call it, so that the portal can show what breaks when that service changes. (Requirement FR-003)

As a platform administrator, I want every registered service's health endpoint probed at a fixed 30-second interval at a scale of 2,000 services, so that I always have fresh evidence of which services are up. (Requirement FR-001 · NFR-002)

As a DevOps engineer, I want each service's published OpenAPI/Swagger document parsed and stored as the latest version, so that the documentation in the portal always matches what the service exposes. (Requirement FR-004)

As a DevOps engineer, I want to search every service's operations by service name, path, HTTP method and tag, so that I can find the contract I need without opening five repositories. (Requirement FR-004)

Summary: Configure probes, thresholds and alert channels
Description: As a platform administrator, I want to set the probe interval, timeout, expected HTTP status, consecutive-failure threshold and notification channel per service, so that alerting matches each service's criticality instead of one global default. (Requirement FR-005)

Summary: Enforce admin-only configuration with an audit trail
Description: As a platform administrator, I want only Administrator-role users to change probe and alert settings, with every change appended to an audit log, so that production monitoring changes are accountable. (Requirement FR-005)

As an on-call engineer, I want exactly one downtime alert after the configured number of consecutive failures and one recovery notification when the service returns, so that I am paged once and not spammed. (Requirement FR-005)
As a DevOps engineer, I want a dashboard showing each service's status and rolling 24-hour availability, so that I can spot a degrading service before it pages anyone. (Requirement FR-001)

As a system architect, I want an interactive topology graph of up to 200 services in which selecting a node highlights its upstream and downstream neighbours, so that I can judge blast radius before a change or during an incident. (Requirement FR-003 · NFR-001)
